title: Directional Price Forecasting in the Continuous Intraday Market under Consideration of Neighboring Products and Limit Order Books

extraction.methodology_summary: The paper proposes a directional electricity price forecasting method for hourly products in the European continuous intraday market using classification models such as logistic regression and gradient boosting. The forecasting framework uses a rolling window approach across the ID 3 period, extracting features from recent transactions, limit order books (LOB), and neighboring hourly and quarter-hourly products. Models are iteratively trained and cross-validated across a one-year test set from April 2024 to April 2025 using German EPEX market data.
extraction.universe: German European Power Exchange (EPEX) continuous intraday market hourly power products

key_findings: Features derived from the limit order book (LOB) are the most influential exogenous variables for improving directional price forecast accuracy.
Features from neighboring hourly and quarter-hourly products whose delivery starts within the trading period of the target product enhance forecast accuracy.
Fundamental variables (load and VRE generation forecasts) and system imbalance data provide limited added value for short-term continuous intraday price forecasting.

Gradient boosting generally outperforms logistic regression in terms of directional accuracy, whereas logistic regression achieves higher PnL at high signal strengths due to regularization/better generalization.
limitations: The analysis focuses exclusively on the ID 3 trading period and hourly products.
The test period spans only 2024–2025, which may limit broader generalizability.
Trading strategy profitability was not evaluated via realistic backtesting with LOB execution mechanics.
